title: share-import — case shape (v0.1)
description: Pins the byte mapping of protocol::encode_share_import_blob_raw + protocol::decode_share_import_blob — the MYF1 share-import staging blob codec (OS share-sheet file import; §9.19). A file handed to Myne from the OS share sheet is held in a device-local encrypted queue until the vault unlocks, then drained into the vault's attachment library. The blob seals an arbitrary-binary framed-file record under a device-local wrap_key. The codec is PROVIDER-AGNOSTIC and VAULT-AGNOSTIC: it never runs Argon2id, and binds NEITHER account_number_hash NOR items_key_id (the queue is created while the vault is locked, or from a separate OS share-extension sandbox that does not hold root_key). It binds the per-entry share_id (also the queue filename) via aad_share_import_blob (AAD role 'share-import-blob'); there is NO HKDF SubkeyRole (a root_key-derived KEK would be wrong — the queue must survive while root_key is unavailable). ciphertext_len is variable (plaintext_len + 32), capped at MAX_SHARE_IMPORT_PLAINTEXT_LEN (64 MiB, matching the MYA1 attachment cap); an oversize ciphertext_len is a CiphertextLenOverflow reject before allocation (contrast vault-quickunlock's fixed 64 → CiphertextLenInvalid). The MYF1 magic is a free-pool §10.3 allocation (F=file, MYND-507), implementer-chosen like every family magic. Four case kinds: 'encrypt' (encoder byte output), 'decrypt_ok' (round-trip to the framed-file plaintext), 'decrypt_aead_fail' (non-distinguishing AEAD failure per §6.4, incl. the cross-share_id header flip which is AAD-bound), 'parse_fail' (distinguishable pre-decryption structural reject, one per ShareImportBlobError decode variant). Reference impl: protocol/src/share_import_blob.rs (main myne repository); spec: docs/spec/protocol.md §9.19 + §5.2.

vector_id.description: Stable identifier of the form 'share-import/v0.1/<descriptive-slug>'. Immutable once shipped — downstream test runners may reference these strings.

oneOf.title: encrypt — pin the encoder's byte output

input_wrap_key_hex.description: 32-byte device-local wrap_key (hex), supplied DIRECTLY. The codec is provider-agnostic — it never derives this key; it is a random 32-byte value held in the OS keychain / Android Keystore.

input_share_id_hex.description: 16-byte share_id (hex) — 16 random bytes that are ALSO the queue filename. Written into the public header at offset 5 AND bound into the 49-byte AAD via aad_share_import_blob (role string 'share-import-blob'), so a tampered header share_id fails AEAD. This is the swap/duplicate protection for the queue directory.

input_plaintext_hex.description: The framed-file record as arbitrary binary bytes (hex), empty allowed. The codec is byte-transparent (this may be genuinely non-UTF-8). Arbitrary length up to MAX_SHARE_IMPORT_PLAINTEXT_LEN (64 MiB); this is the AEAD plaintext.

input_nonce_hex.description: 24-byte XChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce (hex). Production callers source from OS CSPRNG; vectors pin a constant.

expected_share_import_blob_hex.description: Full encoder output, hex-encoded lowercase. Variable length = 49-byte header + plaintext_len + 32-byte CTX tag. Decoders compare byte-equal.

oneOf.title: decrypt_ok — pin the decoder's successful round-trip

expected_plaintext_hex.description: The recovered framed-file record as arbitrary binary bytes (hex). Note the decoder reads share_id from the blob's own header (it is not a separate decode input).

oneOf.title: decrypt_aead_fail — pin the non-distinguishing failure surface

expected_kind.description: The decoder MUST report a non-distinguishing AEAD failure (Rust reference: ShareImportBlobError::CannotDecrypt). Implementations MUST NOT distinguish tampered ciphertext/tag vs wrong wrap_key vs cross-share_id (a flipped header share_id, which is AAD-bound) beyond the single 'cannot decrypt' outcome (spec §6.4). Structurally distinguishable rejects (bad magic, oversize ciphertext_len, etc.) are pinned separately under case_kind 'parse_fail'.

oneOf.title: parse_fail — pin a distinguishable pre-decryption structural reject

input_blob_hex.description: A structurally malformed blob (hex), empty allowed. The decoder rejects it BEFORE attempting any decryption — magic / protocol_version / ciphertext_len checks all run before the AEAD stage (spec §9.19.3 magic-byte-before-decrypt discipline).

expected_error.description: The specific structural reject the decoder MUST surface (Rust reference: ShareImportBlobError::{MagicMismatch, ProtocolVersionMismatch, CiphertextLenOverflow, HeaderTooShort, CiphertextTruncated}). NOTE this is 'ciphertext_len_overflow' (unlike vault-quickunlock's 'ciphertext_len_invalid'): the share-import ciphertext_len is VARIABLE with a 64 MiB cap, so an oversize length is an overflow reject before allocation. A flipped-but-structurally-valid header share_id is a decrypt_aead_fail, not a parse_fail.
